OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Integration for Excel and Google Sheets

Overview

OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets, a spreadsheet‑native AI experience that appears as a sidebar inside the respective applications. The feature lets users create, modify and understand spreadsheets using natural‑language prompts, and it is available to a wide range of accounts.

Availability and User Plans

The integration is offered globally to Business, Enterprise, Education and K‑12 customers, as well as to individual users on the Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. Free and Go accounts receive limited usage, while Plus and Pro provide access subject to an agentic usage limit that is shared with other AI tools. Business and Enterprise customers can monitor consumption and purchase additional credits. A free preview for Education and K‑12 users runs until June 2 2026; after that, usage follows each plan’s credit and usage terms.

How the Feature Works

When installed, the ChatGPT add‑in appears as a sidebar in Excel or Google Sheets. It can:

  • Build new trackers, budgets, plans or templates from scratch.
  • Clean messy sheets by standardizing formatting, fixing duplicate labels and repairing broken formulas.
  • Explain unfamiliar spreadsheets, highlighting assumptions, drivers and key formulas.
  • Update models when input values change and summarize the modifications.
  • Review reporting, KPI and forecasting work and generate summaries.

These capabilities are demonstrated through example prompts such as “Create a formatted monthly budget with categories, totals and charts” or “Explain the formula chain in cell B145 and propose a fix.”

Installation Steps

For Excel

  1. Add the ChatGPT add‑in from the Microsoft Marketplace and open it from the ribbon.
  2. Sign in with the same ChatGPT account used for Codex. If your organization uses a workspace, select the matching workspace in both places.
  3. Open the desired workbook, launch the ChatGPT desktop app, select Codex, and mention @Microsoft Excel or ask Codex to work with the open file.
  4. Ensure the add‑in’s “Allow Codex control” option is enabled in the more‑options menu (•••).
  5. Keep the workbook and add‑in pane open, then ask Codex to locate the workbook again.

For Google Sheets

  1. Install the add‑on from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
  2. Open ChatGPT from the Extensions menu and sign in with a supported account.
  3. If your organization uses role‑based access control, an admin must enable the add‑on.
  4. Select ChatGPT for Excel and Sheets and enable it.

Both platforms require the add‑in and Codex to be signed into the same ChatGPT account; otherwise the add‑in will not start.

Practical Implications

The AI sidebar can reduce manual effort for finance, operations and data‑analysis teams that routinely work with large, multi‑tab workbooks. By describing desired changes in plain language, users can generate structured tables, update assumptions and produce charts without rewriting formulas. The ability to search the web for data also lets the AI enrich spreadsheets with up‑to‑date information.

However, the feature has limitations. VBA macros and other advanced Excel scripting may not be fully supported, and certain actions may require direct user control of the workbook. Data residency and inference controls are available only where the enterprise plan permits them. Users should review all generated formulas, calculations and citations before relying on the output, and for critical work duplicate the file first to allow reverting changes.

Verification and Support

OpenAI’s Help Center provides the official guidance shown above. To confirm the announcement, check the URL https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001063-chatgpt-for-excel-and-google-sheets The article states that the feature is “available globally” and lists the supported user plans. Administrators can verify enablement through workspace settings, and they can monitor usage via the Compliance API. If an “add‑in could not be started” error appears during single sign‑on, the cause is typically an outdated SSO callback URL; updating the enterprise application’s default URL in the identity provider resolves the issue.

Conclusion

ChatGPT’s integration with Excel and Google Sheets brings AI‑driven assistance directly into familiar spreadsheet environments. While the rollout is extensive and includes free previews for many user categories, users must respect usage limits, verify outputs, and ensure proper account and workspace configuration before deploying at scale.
